utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody here. Good early morning. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Case number IT-04-84-PT, the Prosecutor versus Haradinaj, Balaj, and Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Thank you. And then I should ask Mr. Balaj, can you hear what's going on in a language which you understand? THE ACCUSED BALAJ: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Brahimaj, the same question to you: Do you understand what's going on? Is it translated to you in a language you understand? THE ACCUSED BRAHIMAJ: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Then we should have the appearance from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: My name is Moore. I'm senior trial attorney. I'm assisted this morning by Ms. Marie Tuma and Mr. Hasan Younis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Thank you. And from Mr. Haradinaj's defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: My name is Ben Emmerson. I'm lead counsel for Mr. Haradinaj and I'm appearing today with Mr. Rodney Dixon, co-counsel, and Mr. Michael O'Reilly, Defence coordinator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Thank you. And appearance for Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Gregor Guy-Smith, appearing on behalf of Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Thank you. And for Mr. Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Richard Harvey and I represent Lahi Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Thank you. So, so far no surprises. Then I should mention also, for the public, that the reason for such a Status Conference is that it follows from Rule 65 bis of our -- the Tribunal's Rules, that a Trial Chamber shall convene a Status Conference within 120 days the initial appearance of the accused in order to organise exchanges between the parties so as to ensure an expeditious preparation for trial and to review the status of the accused's case and to allow the accused the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including his mental and physical condition and matters relating to detention. So that's the reasons. And we have looked upon if there is any outstanding motions. There is none, but during the Rule 65 ter meeting, which took place yesterday, it was announced, I can see, from the Defence of Mr. Haradinaj that by the 14th of August they will file a motion seeking an amendment to the conditions for the provisional release with a request for hearing in the week of the 12th September. And now, is that so?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: That's correct. And then, of course, it -- there will be a need for an answer from the Prosecution, I suppose, and that means that we probably -- this will go on in the summer recess to have some dates, some limitations announced. I'm probably a little surprised that it will be that early that we'll have a motion from the Defence, but you have taken into account the 90 days which is mentioned, I suppose, in the conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. The time that we propose for the hearing is beyond the 90-day period identified in the conditions, and the date of the 14th of August is simply working back from a workable hearing date. So certainly the 12th of September is comfortably beyond the 90-day period that the Chamber identified in the conditions for provisional release relating to political activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Yes. Very well, then. Then we'll go along with this plan. And for Mr. Brahimaj, it was announced that they will file a motion for provisional release by the end of July. This certainly will be in the middle of the recess, of course, and I don't know if it would be easier, for practical reasons, if you delayed that a bit, or else, of course, we will put a time limit on Prosecution, on their response, which would allow, for practical reasons, not to have anybody sitting in the recess period for that matter. But what is the position of the Defence there?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me just make clear. The target date of the end of July is one that I essentially have imposed on myself in order to provide the Prosecution with sufficient time to investigate the proposed conditions that we will be suggesting should meet the requirements of the Court for provisional release. It is our expectation, and we do this from the point of view of -- with an eye to saving court time and dealing with all matters as expeditiously as possible, that the hearing for that provisional release application could take place in the same week and perhaps on the same day as that on which the Court considers the application on behalf of Mr. Haradinaj to amend his conditions of provisional release.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Okay. That's very reasonable, I suppose. And that means that if we set a time limit to the 1st of August, which I know has been discussed with the chief legal officer, and then the Prosecution's response to that to the 22nd of August, then everything should be able to go along the idea you have had. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: From my standpoint, that's perfectly acceptable. I don't know whether Mr. Moore has any difficulties with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I would have thought that that would be an appropriate time. The problem that we would have is that we are not in a position to know exactly the conditions that may be suggested by the Defence, but on a preliminary view I would have thought that period would be appropriate. If, however, it does create difficulties, then of course we would seek to have an extension of time in relation to that, but we would try for the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you. Thank you. Let it be so. So we know that the Defence of Mr. Haradinaj have mentioned that they will not file preliminary motions in -- pursuant to Rule 72 of the Rules, and the Defence of the two other accused have not filed such motions within the prescribed time limit, so there is no problem there. Likewise, it can be noticed that the Prosecution have disclosed in relation to Rule 66(A)(i), and that disclosure has been completed on the 5th of May, 2005, so there is no problem there. Then I have been told that the parties, as they should, have, during the 65 ter meeting, discussed how this case could be prepared for the trial. And of course, as everybody knows, this Trial Chamber tries really to handle the cases as rapidly as possible, but for the time being the parties have the following work plan in mind: The Prosecution should complete its Rule 66(A)(ii) disclosure by May next year. The parties will discuss possible agreed facts roughly around May, July 2006. The scheduling of pre-trial briefs will take place in late autumn 2006. The start of trial is envisaged as being January 2007, but that's, of course, depending on a Bench being available. The length of trial, as far as it can be estimated at the moment, would roughly be around 18 months, but certainly we want to see if it can't be shorter, but the parties, as far as I understand, do not foresee a possibility for the trial to run for less than 12 months. That, of course, is something which will be discussed in details when the relevant time comes. So that seems to be the very easy task this morning, to make this clear. Does anybody have anything to -- further to mention, to raise this morning? Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Just two brief matters, Your Honour. One I should say, as I did yesterday in our conference, that the reason why no provisional release application has been made so far on behalf of Mr. Brahimaj was because he and I both discussed this matter and we agreed that it was wise to allow a reasonable period after the release of Mr. Haradinaj to -- so that the Court and all parties could be assured that that release did not lead to any cause for concern and so that we could monitor the situation in Kosovo, and that's why we haven't made an application until now. We thought that was the most reasonable approach to take. Secondly, and it's a matter that's been one of concern for some time, as you indicated in your opening remarks, one of the purposes of today's hearing is to assure the physical and mental well-being of the defendants, and I raise -- with some diffidence I raise the question of my client's rheumatism which has been troubling him for a considerable period of time. He has a five-year history of suffering from rheumatism. I'm just realising that I'm speaking perhaps a little quickly. I beg your pardon. He has seen the doctor in the Detention Unit, but I don't -- I have the sense from him, let me put it this way, that he does not believe that this doctor is taking -- has any specialisation in the field of rheumatism, and he feels that it would be appropriate to have a complete physical medical exam. I raise that, Your Honour, because you are the ultimate authority in these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm fully aware that the climate here is not best for rheumatism. I can assure you I'm aware of that. But we will take note of this, and I will consult with the right authority on this matter, but anyhow, it has been noticed that there is this complaint or what you would call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I would say concern rather than complaint, but thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Thank you. And then I take it that after this there probably is no matter to raise relating -- further matter to raise relating the state of health or condition of detention for the two detainees. I see that you nod, so I take that for everybody. So we can then conclude this conference, and the court stands adjourned. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: [The accused Haradinaj not present in Court]
